concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n(lg n)^(1-κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: big-O bound
symbols.meaning: The asymptotic upper bound notation: a function is O(g) when it is at most a constant times g for all large inputs.

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers.

symbols.name: binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1, so that lg n = max{ceil(log2 n), 1}.

symbols.name: power-saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^(-182) by which the logarithmic factor is reduced below lg n.

concepts.gloss: A deterministic multitape Turing machine that multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n(lg n)^(1-κ)) worst-case time for a fixed κ = 2^(-182) > 0, beating the n log n conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers

concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Notation O(g) for the set of functions bounded above by a constant multiple of g for all sufficiently large inputs.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, each with its own head that moves at most one cell per step.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with a, b real and i² = −1, used for the roots of unity and the coefficients of the transforms.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Expressions a₀ + a₁y + … + a_k y^k over a coefficient ring, with the usual addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture
concepts.gloss: The conjecture of Schönhage and Strassen that n log n is the optimal order of growth of the time to multiply two n-bit integers on a multitape Turing machine.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplication
aliases: Harvey and van der Hoeven multiplier
concepts.gloss: The unconditional O(n log n) multiplication algorithm on a multitape Turing machine, used in this result as an ordinary subroutine.

evidence.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper

concepts.name: Matrix rank
concepts.gloss: The rank of a matrix is the maximum number of linearly independent rows or columns; the number of nonzero pivots in elimination.

evidence.quote: Each step isolates a rank-one block

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The map sending a length-n sequence to its values at the n-th roots of unity, i.e. the sums of the sequence weighted by powers of a root of unity.

evidence.quote: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for

concepts.name: Primitive roots of unity
concepts.gloss: A complex number ω is a primitive n-th root of unity when ω^n = 1 and no smaller positive power equals 1.

evidence.quote: serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of two sequences in which indices are taken modulo a fixed length, so each coefficient of the result is a sum of products over residues.

evidence.quote: into normalized cyclic convolution

concepts.name: Multiplication as convolution of digits
concepts.gloss: Writing each integer in radix 2^b digits so that the integer product becomes a convolution of the digit sequences, which is then carried back to binary.

evidence.quote: reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: A rearrangement that places a digit sequence on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes while preserving convolution, implemented with address interchanges.

evidence.quote: by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: An identity that expresses a Fourier transform of length given by a prime as a multidimensional transform with power-of-two axis lengths, with the source and target permutations kept in the identity.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity
concepts.gloss: The identity that converts a Fourier transform into a cyclic convolution by multiplying by chirp factors before and after it.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The variable of the polynomial ring whose powers serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of coefficients in the coefficient list of one polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials in y reduced modulo y^r + 1, where multiplying by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A transform over a polynomial ring in which the roots of unity are powers of y, so that each transform stage uses only signed shifts and butterfly additions.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing
concepts.gloss: Encoding a polynomial with bounded signed coefficients as an integer by evaluating it at a large power of two, so that polynomial products become integer products.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Butterfly operation
concepts.gloss: The two-point map (u, v) ↦ ((u + v)/2, (u − v)/2) applied to a pair of values, the basic step of a fast transform.

evidence.quote: two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: A butterfly operation applied at once on one selected address bit of every record, with exact Gaussian dyadic intermediates and a single truncation after the layer.

evidence.quote: simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of the numerical arrays

concepts.name: Linear network with restored auxiliary values
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network that exchanges banks of values with prescribed signs and restores every auxiliary value, with each gate acting on the stored array through a frame operator that cancels between edges.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two

concepts.name: Lower-triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: The factorization A = E₁ΠE₂ of a rational matrix into invertible lower-triangular factors and a partial permutation matrix with one 1 per pivot.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The permutation (H, D) ↦ (H + AD, D) on two ordered groups of address fields, which is performed with as many pairwise interchanges as the rank of A.

evidence.quote: two fields, written as vectors $H,D$ over a common residue ring, are

concepts.name: Fast address interchange
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that swaps two disjoint contiguous address fields of an array in time O(V u^τ) for width u, computed through XOR combinations of intermediate data.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields

concepts.name: Recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: The mechanism in which a network with s smaller calls on W roles and parameter m gives a recursion with cost ratio s/W < m, so that repeated recursion saves a power of the parameter.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding
concepts.gloss: The step in which the approximate convolution coefficients are rounded to integers, provided the error is strictly below 1/2, and carries are then propagated to give the exact binary product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers in which a and b are identified when they differ by a multiple of a fixed modulus c, written a ≡ b (mod c).

concepts.name: Prime numbers and greatest common divisors
concepts.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself, and gcd(a, b) is the largest integer dividing both a and b; a and b are coprime when their gcd is 1.

concepts.name: Arithmetic modulo 2 and XOR
concepts.gloss: The set {0, 1} with addition given by exclusive-or (sum modulo 2) and multiplication given by AND, which is the arithmetic of bits and parity.

concepts.name: Dyadic rationals
concepts.gloss: Rational numbers of the form a/2^k with a an integer and k a nonnegative integer, i.e. the numbers with finite binary expansions.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, bases and dimension
concepts.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication; a basis is a linearly independent spanning set, and the dimension is the number of vectors in any basis.

concepts.name: Linear maps, matrix operations and invertibility
concepts.gloss: A linear map sends sums to sums and scalar multiples to scalar multiples and is represented by a matrix; a square matrix is invertible when it has a two-sided inverse, and the kernel is the set of vectors sent to zero.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.gloss: The procedure that reduces a matrix by elementary row operations to echelon form, whose pivots determine solutions and rank.

concepts.name: Triangular matrices
concepts.gloss: A square matrix whose entries above (lower-triangular) or below (upper-triangular) the diagonal are all zero.

concepts.name: Dot product and orthogonality in R^n
concepts.gloss: The dot product of two real vectors is the sum of products of corresponding entries; two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero, and an orthonormal basis consists of mutually orthogonal unit vectors.

concepts.name: Permutations of a finite set
concepts.gloss: A bijection from a finite set of indices to itself, which rearranges the entries of a sequence or array.

concepts.name: Finite sets, subsets and intersections
concepts.gloss: The intersection of two sets is the set of their common elements, the cardinality counts elements, and the binomial coefficient (n choose k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set.

concepts.name: Graphs
aliases: source and sink vertices of the network
concepts.gloss: A graph is a set of vertices together with a set of edges, each joining two vertices, and two vertices are adjacent when they are joined by an edge.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for all integers n by proving a base case and that the statement for smaller values implies it for n.

concepts.name: Recurrence relations and divide-and-conquer recursion
concepts.gloss: An equation that defines a quantity, such as the running time of a recursive algorithm, in terms of its values on smaller inputs.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The floor of x is the largest integer not exceeding x and the ceiling is the smallest integer not less than x.

concepts.name: Logarithms base 2
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg x is the exponent to which 2 must be raised to give x, which is the number of binary digits needed to represent x up to one.

concepts.name: Big-Omega and big-Theta notation
concepts.gloss: f = Ω(g) means f is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of g for all large inputs, and f = Θ(g) means f is both O(g) and Ω(g).

concepts.name: Limits and convergence of sequences and series
concepts.gloss: A sequence converges to L when its terms eventually stay arbitrarily close to L, and a series converges when its partial sums converge.

concepts.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
concepts.gloss: The series a + ar + ar^2 + ... whose partial sums equal a(1 - r^(k+1))/(1 - r), converging when |r| < 1 to a/(1 - r).

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: The iteration x_{k+1} = x_k - f(x_k)/f'(x_k) that approximates a root of f by repeatedly following tangent lines.

concepts.name: Worst-case time complexity of a Turing machine
concepts.gloss: For a Turing machine, the maximum number of steps it takes on any input of length n, viewed as a function of n.

concepts.name: Tensor product
concepts.gloss: The tensor product V ⊗ W of two vector spaces, whose basis consists of all pairs of basis vectors of V and W, together with the tensor product A ⊗ B of linear maps, which acts on each coordinate separately.

evidence.quote: The intended operation is the tensor product

address-interchange.name: stored bit volume
address-interchange.meaning: The number of data bits the array holds.
address-interchange.quote: $V$ is the stored bit volume, the number of data bits the array holds.

address-interchange.name: field width
address-interchange.meaning: The number of address bits in one field.
address-interchange.quote: $u$ is the width of each field, the number of address bits in one field; the letter $u$ changes meaning here.

address-interchange.name: width exponent
address-interchange.meaning: A fixed exponent with 0 < tau < 1 in the cost bound O(V u^tau).

address-interchange.name: matrix size
address-interchange.meaning: The size of the network's matrices; each field splits into d pieces.
address-interchange.quote: Let $d\ge2$ be the size of the network's matrices; a field splits into $d$ pieces of width $u/d$.

address-interchange.name: wire count
address-interchange.meaning: The number of wires of the network, scratch wires included.
address-interchange.quote: Its $W$ wires, scratch wires included, each carry rows of volume $V/W$.

address-interchange.name: network edge
address-interchange.meaning: An edge of the linear network, running from its tail to its head.
address-interchange.quote: Each edge $e$ changes that shear by $G_e$, the difference of its end-vertex matrices, by the interchanges above.

address-interchange.name: edge matrix difference
address-interchange.meaning: The difference of the matrices at the two ends of the edge e, which changes the shear.
address-interchange.quote: Each edge $e$ changes that shear by $G_e$, the difference of its end-vertex matrices, by the interchanges above.

address-interchange.name: calls per level
address-interchange.meaning: The number of interchange calls made in one level, summed over the edges.
address-interchange.quote: Summing over edges, one level makes $R=\sum_e\operatorname{rank}G_e$ calls, each on volume $V/W$ and width $u/d$.

address-interchange.name: time per bit
address-interchange.meaning: The time per stored bit of an array of field width u.
address-interchange.quote: Let $\varphi(u)$ be the time per stored bit at width $u$.

address-interchange.name: level constant
address-interchange.meaning: A constant bounding the work of one level, per stored bit.
address-interchange.quote: Each level's own work is $CV$ for a constant $C$, so dividing by $V$ gives $\varphi(u)\le\gamma\varphi(u/d)+C$, with $\gamma=R/W$.

address-interchange.name: cost ratio
address-interchange.meaning: The ratio R/W of the calls per level to the wires, which multiplies the cost of the recursion.
address-interchange.quote: Each level's own work is $CV$ for a constant $C$, so dividing by $V$ gives $\varphi(u)\le\gamma\varphi(u/d)+C$, with $\gamma=R/W$.

address-interchange.name: number of levels
address-interchange.meaning: The number of levels of the recursion needed to reach width 1.
address-interchange.quote: Let $\ell=\log_d u$ be the number of levels; $\ell$ levels reach width 1, where a single-digit swap gives $\varphi(1)=O(1)$.

address-shear.name: first address group
address-shear.meaning: The first group of address fields, a vector over a common residue ring with one entry for each row of A.
address-shear.quote: Here $H$ is the first group, a vector over a common residue ring (the integers with arithmetic taken modulo a fixed number), with one entry for each row of $A$.

address-shear.name: second address group
address-shear.meaning: The second group of address fields, with one entry for each column of A.
address-shear.quote: $D$ is the second group, with one entry for each column of $A$.

address-shear.name: field index of H
address-shear.meaning: An index running over the fields of H, labelling the row of a 1 in Π.
address-shear.quote: On this page $s$ and $t$ take new meanings: $s$ indexes the fields of $H$ and $t$ the fields of $D$, and a 1 in row $s$ and column $t$ of $\Pi$ calls for $H_s\leftarrow H_s+D_t$.

address-shear.name: field index of D
address-shear.meaning: An index running over the fields of D, labelling the column of a 1 in Π.
address-shear.quote: On this page $s$ and $t$ take new meanings: $s$ indexes the fields of $H$ and $t$ the fields of $D$, and a 1 in row $s$ and column $t$ of $\Pi$ calls for $H_s\leftarrow H_s+D_t$.

bluestein-chirp.name: chirp base
bluestein-chirp.meaning: The complex number $\zeta=e^{\pi i/n}$, whose powers are the chirp factors.
bluestein-chirp.quote: Let $\zeta=e^{\pi i/n}$, so that $\zeta^2=\omega$ and $\zeta^n=-1$; $\zeta$ is the chirp base, and its powers are the chirp factors.

bluestein-chirp.name: chirp offset
bluestein-chirp.meaning: The integer offset $k-j$ between an output index and an input index, as used in the chirp sum.

bluestein-chirp.name: coefficient position
bluestein-chirp.meaning: A coefficient position of the ring, running from 0 to n-1.
bluestein-chirp.quote: Let $\sigma$ be a coefficient position, from $0$ to $n-1$.

bluestein-chirp.name: wrapped coefficient
bluestein-chirp.meaning: The coefficient at $y^{\sigma+n}$ in the twisted product, which wraps around to position $\sigma$.
bluestein-chirp.quote: Let $\delta$ be the coefficient at $y^{\sigma+n}$ in the twisted product.

butterfly-operation.name: first input value
butterfly-operation.meaning: The first of the two input values that the butterfly maps.
butterfly-operation.quote: Let $u$ and $v$ be two input values, and let $H_0$ denote the butterfly map, so that $H_0(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+v}{2},\frac{u-v}{2}\right)$.

butterfly-operation.name: second input value
butterfly-operation.meaning: The second of the two input values that the butterfly maps.
butterfly-operation.quote: Let $u$ and $v$ be two input values, and let $H_0$ denote the butterfly map, so that $H_0(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+v}{2},\frac{u-v}{2}\right)$.

butterfly-operation.name: butterfly map
butterfly-operation.meaning: The two-point map sending a pair of values to its half-sum and half-difference.
butterfly-operation.quote: Let $u$ and $v$ be two input values, and let $H_0$ denote the butterfly map, so that $H_0(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+v}{2},\frac{u-v}{2}\right)$.

butterfly-operation.name: identity matrix
butterfly-operation.meaning: The $2\times 2$ identity matrix, which leaves every pair unchanged.
butterfly-operation.quote: Squaring the matrix gives $H_0^2=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}=\frac12 I$, where $I$ denotes the $2\times 2$ identity matrix.

chinese-remainder-address-map.name: coefficient count
chinese-remainder-address-map.meaning: The number of coefficients in the list being placed on the axes.
chinese-remainder-address-map.quote: Let $N$ be the number of coefficients in the list, and let $P$ be the number of axes.

chinese-remainder-address-map.name: axis count
chinese-remainder-address-map.meaning: The number of prime cyclic axes on which the coefficient list is placed.
chinese-remainder-address-map.quote: Let $N$ be the number of coefficients in the list, and let $P$ be the number of axes.

chinese-remainder-address-map.name: axis length
chinese-remainder-address-map.meaning: The prime length of the first axis; the lengths $L_1,\dots,L_P$ are pairwise distinct primes.
chinese-remainder-address-map.quote: Let $L_1,\dots,L_P$ be the prime lengths of the axes, pairwise distinct, so that $N = L_1 L_2 \cdots L_P$.

chinese-remainder-address-map.name: list position
chinese-remainder-address-map.meaning: A position in the coefficient list, an integer from 0 to N-1.
chinese-remainder-address-map.quote: Let $J$ be a position in the list, running from $0$ to $N-1$.

convolution-reduction.name: digit width
convolution-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one digit, a count of bits.
convolution-reduction.quote: Let $b$ be the number of bits in one digit; here $b$ does not mean the second input sequence of the cyclic convolution page.

convolution-reduction.name: digit count
convolution-reduction.meaning: The number of digits in each input, a count of digits.
convolution-reduction.quote: Let $m$ be the number of digits in each input.

convolution-reduction.name: first input integer
convolution-reduction.meaning: The first of the two integers being multiplied.
convolution-reduction.quote: Let $U$ be the first input and $V$ the second.

convolution-reduction.name: second input integer
convolution-reduction.meaning: The second of the two integers being multiplied.
convolution-reduction.quote: Let $U$ be the first input and $V$ the second.

cyclic-convolution.name: formal variable
cyclic-convolution.meaning: A formal variable, an indeterminate not evaluated at any number, used as the placeholder of the polynomials a(x) and b(x).
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $x$ be a formal variable, an indeterminate not evaluated at any number, and write $a(x) = \sum_j a_j x^j$ and $b(x) = \sum_j b_j x^j$.

cyclic-convolution.name: sequence length
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each input sequence, so both sequences have length r.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $a = (a_0, \ldots, a_{r-1})$ and $b = (b_0, \ldots, b_{r-1})$ be two complex sequences of length $r$, where $r$ is the number of complex coefficients in each.

cyclic-convolution.name: second input sequence
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The second of the two input sequences, a list of r complex numbers.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $a = (a_0, \ldots, a_{r-1})$ and $b = (b_0, \ldots, b_{r-1})$ be two complex sequences of length $r$, where $r$ is the number of complex coefficients in each.

cyclic-convolution.name: cyclic convolution
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The cyclic convolution of a and b, a sequence of r complex coefficients.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Their cyclic convolution, written $c = a \circledast b$, is the length-$r$ sequence with coefficients

cyclic-convolution.name: term index of b
cyclic-convolution.meaning: An index running over 0 to r-1 that labels the terms of b in the reduced product.
cyclic-convolution.quote: In general, let $l$ be the index of a term of $b$, running over $\{0, \ldots, r-1\}$.

fourier-transform.name: sequence length
fourier-transform.meaning: The count of entries in the input sequence $a$, and so the number of output entries and the order of the root $\omega$ in this transform.
fourier-transform.quote: The input sequence is $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$, a list of complex numbers, where $n$ is its length.

fourier-transform.name: input sequence
fourier-transform.meaning: The input sequence $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of $n$ complex numbers, the coefficient list of the polynomial $p$.
fourier-transform.quote: The input sequence is $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$, a list of complex numbers, where $n$ is its length.

fourier-transform.name: input position
fourier-transform.meaning: The index of an input entry $a_j$, running from $0$ to $n-1$; on this page it is not the power exponent it denotes on the roots-of-unity page.
fourier-transform.quote: Here $j$ is the input position, running from $0$ to $n-1$, and $k$ is the output position, running over the same range.

fourier-transform.name: output position
fourier-transform.meaning: The index of an output entry $\hat a_k$, running from $0$ to $n-1$; on this page it is not the power exponent it denotes on the roots-of-unity page.
fourier-transform.quote: Here $j$ is the input position, running from $0$ to $n-1$, and $k$ is the output position, running over the same range.

fourier-transform.name: transform of a
fourier-transform.meaning: The output sequence $\hat a = (\hat a_0, \dots, \hat a_{n-1})$, the discrete Fourier transform of $a$.
fourier-transform.quote: The output sequence is $\hat a = (\hat a_0, \dots, \hat a_{n-1})$, the transform of $a$, with entries given by the formula below.

fourier-transform.name: coefficient polynomial
fourier-transform.meaning: The polynomial $p(x)$ whose coefficient list is $a$.
fourier-transform.quote: Let $p(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_j x^j$ be the polynomial with coefficient list $a$, where $x$ is a formal variable, a placeholder for a number to be substituted.

fourier-transform.name: formal variable
fourier-transform.meaning: The formal variable of the polynomial $p$, a placeholder for a number to be substituted.
fourier-transform.quote: Let $p(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_j x^j$ be the polynomial with coefficient list $a$, where $x$ is a formal variable, a placeholder for a number to be substituted.

gaussian-resampling.name: prime length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The prime length of the sequence z, a count of its complex entries.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $q$ be a prime, the length of a sequence $z=(z_0,\dots,z_{q-1})$ of complex numbers.

gaussian-resampling.name: input sequence
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The sequence of q complex numbers that the transform acts on.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $q$ be a prime, the length of a sequence $z=(z_0,\dots,z_{q-1})$ of complex numbers.

gaussian-resampling.name: normalized transform
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length q, with the scaling 1/q.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) $F_q$ of length $q$ as a transform over power-of-two axes.

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The length of the source transform, a count of its entries.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $n_0<n_1$ be integers, the lengths of the source and target transforms, with $\gcd(n_0,n_1)=1$ and $n_1$ a power of two.

gaussian-resampling.name: target length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The length of the target transform, a power of two that counts its entries.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $n_0<n_1$ be integers, the lengths of the source and target transforms, with $\gcd(n_0,n_1)=1$ and $n_1$ a power of two.

gaussian-resampling.name: source permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The source coordinate permutation, which reorders the outputs of the source transform.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $F_{n_0}$ and $F_{n_1}$ be their normalized transforms, and let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the source and target coordinate permutations, which reorder the outputs of $F_{n_0}$ and $F_{n_1}$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The target coordinate permutation, which reorders the outputs of the target transform.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $F_{n_0}$ and $F_{n_1}$ be their normalized transforms, and let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the source and target coordinate permutations, which reorder the outputs of $F_{n_0}$ and $F_{n_1}$.

gaussian-resampling.name: identity constant
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The power-of-two constant on the right side of the identity.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $K=2^{2\alpha^2}$ be a power of two, where $\alpha\ge 2$ is an integer parameter of the construction.

gaussian-resampling.name: construction parameter
gaussian-resampling.meaning: An integer parameter of the construction, at least 2, that fixes K.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $K=2^{2\alpha^2}$ be a power of two, where $\alpha\ge 2$ is an integer parameter of the construction.

gaussian-resampling.name: first contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A linear contraction from the n_0-coordinate space to the n_1-coordinate space.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Here $M_1:\mathbb C^{n_0}\to\mathbb C^{n_1}$ and $M_2:\mathbb C^{n_1}\to\mathbb C^{n_0}$ are linear contractions, maps that do not increase the size of a vector.

gaussian-resampling.name: second contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A linear contraction from the n_1-coordinate space back to the n_0-coordinate space.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Here $M_1:\mathbb C^{n_0}\to\mathbb C^{n_1}$ and $M_2:\mathbb C^{n_1}\to\mathbb C^{n_0}$ are linear contractions, maps that do not increase the size of a vector.

harvey-hoeven-multiplier.name: exponent gap
harvey-hoeven-multiplier.meaning: A fixed positive constant, $2^{-182}$, by which the logarithmic exponent of the target running time falls below 1.
harvey-hoeven-multiplier.quote: The target's bound is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for a fixed constant $\kappa>0$.

integer-multiplication-target.name: big-O bound
integer-multiplication-target.meaning: The asymptotic upper bound notation: a function is O(g) when it is at most a constant times g for all large inputs.
integer-multiplication-target.quote: Here $O(g)$ means at most a constant times $g$ for all large inputs.

integer-multiplication-target.name: binary logarithm
integer-multiplication-target.meaning: The base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1, so that lg n = max{ceil(log2 n), 1}.
integer-multiplication-target.quote: $\lg n = \max\{\lceil \log_2 n\rceil, 1\}$ is the base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1.

kronecker-packing.name: packed ring element
kronecker-packing.meaning: A ring element with integer coefficients $f_j$, the first of the two elements being packed.
kronecker-packing.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be ring elements with integer coefficients $f_j$ and $g_j$.

kronecker-packing.name: second ring element
kronecker-packing.meaning: A ring element with integer coefficients $g_j$, the second of the two elements being packed.
kronecker-packing.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be ring elements with integer coefficients $f_j$ and $g_j$.

kronecker-packing.name: coefficient bound
kronecker-packing.meaning: A bound on the absolute value of every coefficient of f and g.
kronecker-packing.quote: Let $M$ be a bound on the absolute value of every such coefficient.

kronecker-packing.name: coefficient position
kronecker-packing.meaning: An index running over the r coefficient positions of f and g, from 0 to r-1.
kronecker-packing.quote: The index $j$ runs over the $r$ coefficient positions, $0 \le j < r$.

kronecker-packing.name: product position
kronecker-packing.meaning: An index over the coefficient positions of the unreduced product w.
kronecker-packing.quote: Here $k$ also indexes coefficient positions, not transform positions.

kronecker-packing.name: packing base
kronecker-packing.meaning: A power of two, larger than 2rM^2, at which the coefficient lists are evaluated.
kronecker-packing.quote: Fix a power of two $B$ with $B > 2rM^2$, and call $B$ the packing base.

kronecker-packing.name: packed integer of f
kronecker-packing.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating f at B.
kronecker-packing.quote: The packed integer of $f$ is $F = \sum_j f_j B^j$, which may be negative because the digits are signed.

kronecker-packing.name: packed integer of g
kronecker-packing.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating g at B.
kronecker-packing.quote: Packing $g$ the same way gives the packed integer $G = \sum_j g_j B^j$.

kronecker-packing.name: unreduced product
kronecker-packing.meaning: The product fg before reduction modulo y^r+1, whose coefficients are w_k.
kronecker-packing.quote: Let $w = fg$ be the unreduced product, that is, before reduction modulo $y^r+1$, with coefficients $w_k = \sum_j f_j g_{k-j}$, where $k$ is the power of $y$ and the sum runs over $0 \le k-j < r$.

linear-network-exchange.name: address set
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The finite set of addresses at which every array on the network's wires is indexed.
linear-network-exchange.quote: The values on a wire form an array indexed by a finite address set $\Omega$, the set of addresses at which the network stores values.

linear-network-exchange.name: input role
linear-network-exchange.meaning: An input role, the fixed place where the network takes in one of its values.
linear-network-exchange.quote: An input role is written $w$, and the network carries it to an output role $\rho(w)$.

linear-network-exchange.name: output role map
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The map sending each input role $w$ to the output role $\rho(w)$ that carries it.
linear-network-exchange.quote: An input role is written $w$, and the network carries it to an output role $\rho(w)$.

linear-network-exchange.name: prescribed sign
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The fixed sign, plus or minus one, that the route from input role $w$ applies.

linear-network-exchange.name: frame
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The invertible linear operator on arrays indexed by $\Omega$ attached to the vertex $v$.
linear-network-exchange.quote: Each source, gate and sink $v$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_v$ on arrays indexed by $\Omega$, its *frame*.

linear-network-exchange.name: tail vertex
linear-network-exchange.meaning: A vertex of the network, the vertex where an edge starts.
linear-network-exchange.quote: For vertices $\alpha$ and $\beta$, an edge from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ changes the stored array by $D_\beta D_\alpha^{-1}$ and leaves the logical array fixed.

linear-network-exchange.name: head vertex
linear-network-exchange.meaning: A vertex of the network, the vertex where an edge from $\alpha$ ends.
linear-network-exchange.quote: For vertices $\alpha$ and $\beta$, an edge from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ changes the stored array by $D_\beta D_\alpha^{-1}$ and leaves the logical array fixed.

linear-network-exchange.name: source vertex
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The source vertex where the input role $w$ enters the network.
linear-network-exchange.quote: Here $\mathrm{source}(w)$ is the source vertex where role $w$ enters, and $\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))$ is the sink vertex where output role $\rho(w)$ leaves; the wiring fixes both.

linear-network-exchange.name: sink vertex
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The sink vertex where the output role $\rho(w)$ leaves the network.
linear-network-exchange.quote: Here $\mathrm{source}(w)$ is the source vertex where role $w$ enters, and $\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))$ is the sink vertex where output role $\rho(w)$ leaves; the wiring fixes both.

linear-network-exchange.name: example address
linear-network-exchange.meaning: One address in $\Omega$ at which the worked example is evaluated.
linear-network-exchange.quote: Let $\xi$ be one address, and let the two wires carry the values $\lambda$ and $\mu$ at $\xi$.

linear-network-exchange.name: first example value
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The value on the first wire at the address $\xi$ in the example.
linear-network-exchange.quote: Let $\xi$ be one address, and let the two wires carry the values $\lambda$ and $\mu$ at $\xi$.

linear-network-exchange.name: second example value
linear-network-exchange.meaning: The value on the second wire at the address $\xi$ in the example.
linear-network-exchange.quote: Let $\xi$ be one address, and let the two wires carry the values $\lambda$ and $\mu$ at $\xi$.

lower-triangular-factorization.name: rational matrix
lower-triangular-factorization.meaning: The rational $m\times m$ matrix being factorized.
lower-triangular-factorization.quote: Let $A$ be a rational $m\times m$ matrix, where $m$ is the number of rows of $A$ (here the letter $m$ changes meaning from the earlier digit count).

lower-triangular-factorization.name: row count
lower-triangular-factorization.meaning: The number of rows of $A$, which is also its number of columns.
lower-triangular-factorization.quote: Let $A$ be a rational $m\times m$ matrix, where $m$ is the number of rows of $A$ (here the letter $m$ changes meaning from the earlier digit count).

lower-triangular-factorization.name: rank
lower-triangular-factorization.meaning: The number of ones in $\Pi$, which equals the rank of $A$.
lower-triangular-factorization.quote: The number $a$ of ones in $\Pi$ is set by the [Matrix rank](matrix-rank.md) of $A$.

lower-triangular-factorization.name: left factor
lower-triangular-factorization.meaning: The invertible lower-triangular matrix on the left of the factorization.
lower-triangular-factorization.quote: The factorization is $A=E_1\Pi E_2$, where $E_1$ and $E_2$ are invertible lower-triangular matrices, with zeros above the diagonal and nonzero diagonal entries, and $\Pi$ is a partial permutation matrix: each row and each column holds at most one $1$, and all other entries are $0$.

lower-triangular-factorization.name: right factor
lower-triangular-factorization.meaning: The invertible lower-triangular matrix on the right of the factorization.
lower-triangular-factorization.quote: The factorization is $A=E_1\Pi E_2$, where $E_1$ and $E_2$ are invertible lower-triangular matrices, with zeros above the diagonal and nonzero diagonal entries, and $\Pi$ is a partial permutation matrix: each row and each column holds at most one $1$, and all other entries are $0$.

lower-triangular-factorization.name: partial permutation matrix
lower-triangular-factorization.meaning: The middle factor, a matrix with at most one $1$ in each row and column and zeros elsewhere.
lower-triangular-factorization.quote: The factorization is $A=E_1\Pi E_2$, where $E_1$ and $E_2$ are invertible lower-triangular matrices, with zeros above the diagonal and nonzero diagonal entries, and $\Pi$ is a partial permutation matrix: each row and each column holds at most one $1$, and all other entries are $0$.

matrix-rank.name: real matrix
matrix-rank.meaning: The real matrix whose rank is taken.

nlogn-conjecture.name: input bit length
nlogn-conjecture.meaning: The number of bits in each input integer; the count of bits in one operand.
nlogn-conjecture.quote: Here $n$ is the number of bits in each input integer, and time is worst-case running time as a function of $n$.

nlogn-conjecture.name: exponent gap
nlogn-conjecture.meaning: A fixed positive constant, the gap $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ in the exponent of the logarithm.
nlogn-conjecture.quote: The exponent gap $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ is a fixed positive constant.

polynomial-ring-y.name: ring indeterminate
polynomial-ring-y.meaning: The variable of the polynomial ring, an indeterminate that is not evaluated at any number.
polynomial-ring-y.quote: The variable of the ring is $y$, an indeterminate that is not evaluated at any number.

polynomial-ring-y.name: coefficient count
polynomial-ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in the list of one element of the ring, a power of two.
polynomial-ring-y.quote: The number of complex coefficients in the list of one element is $r$, a power of two.

polynomial-ring-y.name: twist factor
polynomial-ring-y.meaning: A complex $2r$-th root of unity with $\theta^r=-1$, by which the phase twist multiplies the entries of a coefficient list.
polynomial-ring-y.quote: The phase twist multiplies the $j$-th entry of a coefficient list by $\theta^j$, where $\theta$ is the twist factor, a complex $2r$-th root of unity with $\theta^r=-1$.

recursive-power-saving.name: input role count
recursive-power-saving.meaning: The number of input roles of the network, which counts the places where it takes in values, not counting scratch wires.
recursive-power-saving.quote: Let $W$ be the number of input roles of the network, the places where it takes in values, not counting scratch wires.

recursive-power-saving.name: smaller-call count
recursive-power-saving.meaning: The number of smaller calls that one call makes.
recursive-power-saving.quote: Let $s$ be the number of smaller calls that one call makes.

recursive-power-saving.name: call parameter
recursive-power-saving.meaning: The parameter of a call, which counts field digits for the address interchange and selected axes for a numerical layer.
recursive-power-saving.quote: Let $P$ be the parameter of a call, which counts field digits for the interchange and selected axes for a numerical layer.

recursive-power-saving.name: parameter growth factor
recursive-power-saving.meaning: The fixed factor, greater than 1, by which the parameter of a call exceeds the parameter of the smaller calls it makes.
recursive-power-saving.quote: Let $m>1$ be the factor by which the parameter grows: a call at parameter $mP$ makes $s$ calls at parameter $P$.

recursive-power-saving.name: level index
recursive-power-saving.meaning: The index of a level of the recursion, counted from the top level with value 0.
recursive-power-saving.quote: Let $\nu$ be the level index, counted from the top with $\nu=0$.

recursive-power-saving.name: saving exponent
recursive-power-saving.meaning: The exponent of the power saving, the logarithm base m of the cost ratio s/W, which governs the cost of the recursion.
recursive-power-saving.quote: Put $e=\log_m(s/W)$, the exponent of the saving, so $s/W=m^e$ and level $\nu$ costs $Vm^{e\nu}$.

roots-of-unity.name: root order
roots-of-unity.meaning: The order of the root, a positive integer that counts the positions of the transform it labels.
roots-of-unity.quote: Let $n$ be a positive integer, the order of the root.

roots-of-unity.name: primitive root
roots-of-unity.meaning: A primitive $n$-th root of unity, the complex number that labels the positions of a transform.
roots-of-unity.quote: A complex number $\omega$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unity if $\omega^n = 1$ and $\omega^k \neq 1$ for every integer exponent $k$ with $1 \le k < n$.

roots-of-unity.name: power exponent
roots-of-unity.meaning: An integer exponent of the root, marking which power of $\omega$ is meant.
roots-of-unity.quote: A complex number $\omega$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unity if $\omega^n = 1$ and $\omega^k \neq 1$ for every integer exponent $k$ with $1 \le k < n$.

roots-of-unity.name: earlier exponent
roots-of-unity.meaning: An integer exponent of the root, the smaller of two powers compared in the distinctness argument.
roots-of-unity.quote: Suppose $\omega^j = \omega^k$ for integer exponents $j$ and $k$ with $0 \le j < k < n$; here $j$ and $k$ are positions in the list of powers.

rounding-recovery.name: first digit array
rounding-recovery.meaning: The array of radix-2^b digits of the first integer, zero-padded to K entries.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $\psi$ and $\chi$ be the arrays of radix-$2^b$ digits of the two integers, each zero-padded to $K$ entries, where $K$ is the source length, the number of entries of each array.

rounding-recovery.name: second digit array
rounding-recovery.meaning: The array of radix-2^b digits of the second integer, zero-padded to K entries.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $\psi$ and $\chi$ be the arrays of radix-$2^b$ digits of the two integers, each zero-padded to $K$ entries, where $K$ is the source length, the number of entries of each array.

rounding-recovery.name: source length
rounding-recovery.meaning: The number of entries of each zero-padded digit array, which is also the length of the transform.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $\psi$ and $\chi$ be the arrays of radix-$2^b$ digits of the two integers, each zero-padded to $K$ entries, where $K$ is the source length, the number of entries of each array.

rounding-recovery.name: retained permutation
rounding-recovery.meaning: The coordinate permutation retained during resampling, sending an array to its entries at the indices $\eta j$.
rounding-recovery.quote: Resampling retains a coordinate permutation $Q$, where $(Q\psi)_j=\psi_{\eta j}$ for a unit $\eta$ modulo $K$, an integer coprime to $K$.

rounding-recovery.name: permutation unit
rounding-recovery.meaning: An integer coprime to K that defines the permutation Q.
rounding-recovery.quote: Resampling retains a coordinate permutation $Q$, where $(Q\psi)_j=\psi_{\eta j}$ for a unit $\eta$ modulo $K$, an integer coprime to $K$.

rounding-recovery.name: transform of length K
rounding-recovery.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform of length K.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $F_K$ be the discrete Fourier transform of length $K$, and $F_K^+$ the same sum with the opposite sign.

rounding-recovery.name: opposite transform
rounding-recovery.meaning: The same transform as F_K with the opposite sign in the exponent.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $F_K$ be the discrete Fourier transform of length $K$, and $F_K^+$ the same sum with the opposite sign.

rounding-recovery.name: fractional bit count
rounding-recovery.meaning: The number of fractional bits kept by each truncation, equal to 6b.
rounding-recovery.quote: Each truncation keeps $Z=6b$ fractional bits, so it adds error below $2^{-Z}$.

rounding-recovery.name: rounded coefficient
rounding-recovery.meaning: The integer that the j-th computed coefficient approximates, once the known scales are removed.
rounding-recovery.quote: Write $\rho_j$ for the integer that the $j$-th computed coefficient approximates, once the known scales are removed.

rounding-recovery.name: digit
rounding-recovery.meaning: The j-th radix-2^b digit of the integer being formed.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $\delta_j$ be the $j$-th radix-$2^b$ digit of the integer being formed and $\sigma_j$ the carry into position $j$ (the letter $\sigma$ changes meaning here).

rounding-recovery.name: carry
rounding-recovery.meaning: The carry into digit position j when the rounded coefficients are written in radix 2^b.
rounding-recovery.quote: Let $\delta_j$ be the $j$-th radix-$2^b$ digit of the integer being formed and $\sigma_j$ the carry into position $j$ (the letter $\sigma$ changes meaning here).

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: chunk bound
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The largest number of equal-width address chunks that one layer acts on, a count.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $d$ is the largest number of equal-width chunks a layer acts on, and $D \le d$ is the number used in one layer; the letter $D$ changes meaning here.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: chunks per layer
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of selected equal-width address chunks used in one layer, a count, at most d.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $d$ is the largest number of equal-width chunks a layer acts on, and $D \le d$ is the number used in one layer; the letter $D$ changes meaning here.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: layer exponent
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: A fixed exponent below one in the layer's cost bound, so that the cost grows in d more slowly than d itself.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $\lambda'$ is a fixed exponent below one.

synthetic-transform.name: input sequence
synthetic-transform.meaning: The input sequence of the transform, a list of $2r$ ring elements $u_0,\dots,u_{2r-1}$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $u_0,\dots,u_{2r-1}$ be a sequence of ring elements; here $u$ names a sequence, not the first butterfly input of earlier pages.

synthetic-transform.name: second input sequence
synthetic-transform.meaning: The second input sequence, a list of $2r$ ring elements $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ whose transform is multiplied entrywise with that of $u$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

synthetic-transform.name: transform of u
synthetic-transform.meaning: The synthetic transform of $u$, whose entry at frequency $s$ is $\hat u_s$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Its transform has entries $\hat u_s=\sum_{t=0}^{2r-1} y^{st}u_t$.

synthetic-transform.name: input position
synthetic-transform.meaning: The input position in $u$, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $t$ be the input position and $s$ the frequency index, $s=0,\dots,2r-1$.

synthetic-transform.name: frequency index
synthetic-transform.meaning: The frequency index of a transform entry, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $t$ be the input position and $s$ the frequency index, $s=0,\dots,2r-1$.

synthetic-transform.name: pair index
synthetic-transform.meaning: The index of the pair of frequencies $2i$ and $2i+1$, running over $0,\dots,r-1$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Write $i$ for the index of the pair of frequencies $2i$ and $2i+1$, so $i$ runs over $0,\dots,r-1$.

synthetic-transform.name: input position in z
synthetic-transform.meaning: The input position in $z$, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

synthetic-transform.name: output position
synthetic-transform.meaning: The index $h$ of an entry $(u\ast z)_h$ of the cyclic convolution.
synthetic-transform.quote: Let $u\ast z$ be the cyclic convolution of $u$ and $z$, with entries $(u\ast z)_h=\sum_{t+q\equiv h \pmod{2r}} u_tz_q$, where $h$ is the output position.

tensor-product.name: first vector space
tensor-product.meaning: A complex vector space, the first factor of the tensor product.
tensor-product.quote: Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over the complex numbers.

tensor-product.name: second vector space
tensor-product.meaning: A complex vector space, the second factor of the tensor product.
tensor-product.quote: Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over the complex numbers.

tensor-product.name: tensor product
tensor-product.meaning: The operation forming the tensor product of two vector spaces, or of two linear maps.
tensor-product.quote: The tensor product $X\otimes Y$ is a vector space whose basis consists of all pairs $\beta\otimes\gamma$, where $\beta$ is a basis vector of $X$ and $\gamma$ is a basis vector of $Y$.

tensor-product.name: basis vector of X
tensor-product.meaning: A basis vector of X, the first entry of a basis pair of X tensor Y.
tensor-product.quote: The tensor product $X\otimes Y$ is a vector space whose basis consists of all pairs $\beta\otimes\gamma$, where $\beta$ is a basis vector of $X$ and $\gamma$ is a basis vector of $Y$.

tensor-product.name: basis vector of Y
tensor-product.meaning: A basis vector of Y, the second entry of a basis pair of X tensor Y.
tensor-product.quote: The tensor product $X\otimes Y$ is a vector space whose basis consists of all pairs $\beta\otimes\gamma$, where $\beta$ is a basis vector of $X$ and $\gamma$ is a basis vector of $Y$.

tensor-product.name: map on X
tensor-product.meaning: A linear map on X, acting on the first factor of a tensor product of maps.
tensor-product.quote: Given linear maps $S$ on $X$ and $T$ on $Y$, their tensor product $S\otimes T$ is the linear map on $X\otimes Y$ determined by

tensor-product.name: map on Y
tensor-product.meaning: A linear map on Y, acting on the second factor of a tensor product of maps.
tensor-product.quote: Given linear maps $S$ on $X$ and $T$ on $Y$, their tensor product $S\otimes T$ is the linear map on $X\otimes Y$ determined by

tensor-product.name: selected chunk count
tensor-product.meaning: The number of selected chunks, each contributing one selected address bit; here D replaces its earlier meaning.
tensor-product.quote: Let $D$ be the number of selected chunks, each contributing one selected address bit.

address-interchange.quote: The procedure is applied to each [Address shear](address-shear.md) that a layer (one stage of the transform) produces.
The shear is realized by running the [Linear network with restored auxiliary values](linear-network-exchange.md), whose gates act pointwise on the array.

address-shear.quote: The shear is based on [Lower-triangular factorization](lower-triangular-factorization.md), which writes $A = E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1$ and $E_2$ invertible lower-triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation matrix with one 1 per pivot.

The shear is realized in a [Linear network with restored auxiliary values](linear-network-exchange.md), which restores every auxiliary value it uses, so the array holds only the updated fields when the shear ends.

bluestein-chirp.quote: The identity is applied to the middle transform produced by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).

Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites a Fourier transform as a [normalized cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) that is bracketed by multiplications by chirps, where a chirp is a factor whose exponent is quadratic in an index.

butterfly-operation.predicate: is a scaled length-2 case of
butterfly-operation.quote: The butterfly is a scaled length-2 case of the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md).

chinese-remainder-address-map.quote: The map preserves [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of length $N$; the source paper proves this for the placement, which applies here because the axis lengths are distinct primes.
It is implemented by [fast address interchange](address-interchange.md) steps.

convolution-reduction.quote: Multiplication reduces to [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of short integer coefficients.

fourier-transform.quote: The transform is defined using [Primitive roots of unity](roots-of-unity.md): fix a primitive $n$-th root of unity $\omega$.

gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) $F_q$ of length $q$ as a transform over power-of-two axes.
Gaussian resampling operates on the axes produced by the [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md).
Gaussian resampling is carried over by [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) to several axes: tensor products give the same identity for multidimensional transforms.

integer-multiplication-target.quote: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time disproves the [Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture](nlogn-conjecture.md) in this model.
It computes its polynomial products by the [Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplication](harvey-hoeven-multiplier.md) on packed integers from [Signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md).
The power saving follows from [Recursive power saving](recursive-power-saving.md).
The integer product is reduced to a convolution of radix-$2^b$ digit sequences, with carries restored to binary, as in [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md).
The algorithm arranges its digits by the [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md) on distinct prime cyclic axes.
It computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which expresses each prime-length transform through power-of-two axes.
It converts its middle transform by [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) into a normalized cyclic convolution.

integer-multiplication-target.predicate: places its last cyclic coordinate in
integer-multiplication-target.quote: It places its last cyclic coordinate in the [Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md), where its wrap is a signed shift.
It computes its forward transforms by [Synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md), which keep frequency order through their pointwise product.

The algorithm builds each transform level from a [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), which acts on one address bit of every record, and whose cost is $O(V d^{\lambda'})$ for $\lambda'<1$.
The algorithm performs its address permutations by [Fast address interchange](address-interchange.md), whose cost is $O(V u^\tau)$ for $\tau<1$.
The algorithm recovers its exact product by [Exact recovery by rounding](rounding-recovery.md), which rounds the approximate coefficients to integers and propagates carries.

kronecker-packing.quote: Signed Kronecker packing maps each element of [Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md) to a single integer, by evaluating it at a large power of two.
Signed Kronecker packing is an instance of [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md): the coefficients act as digits and the evaluation point as the radix.

linear-network-exchange.quote: Each frame $D_v$ is invertible, so the network has frames of full [matrix rank](matrix-rank.md) on $\Omega$.

lower-triangular-factorization.quote: The number $a$ of ones in $\Pi$ is set by the [Matrix rank](matrix-rank.md) of $A$.

polynomial-ring-y.quote: Multiplication in this ring computes products by a signed form of [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md): the coefficient lists are convolved, and any term that wraps past index $r-1$ returns with a minus sign.

recursive-power-saving.quote: It is built from a [Linear network with restored auxiliary values](linear-network-exchange.md), a fixed network that exchanges two banks of values and restores every auxiliary value.

Applied to the [Fast address interchange](address-interchange.md) with field width $u$ as the parameter, this recursion bounds the cost of the interchange by $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau$ with $e\le\tau<1$. The top parameter is $m^\ell=u$, and since $u\ge 1$, $u^e\le u^\tau$ whenever $e\le\tau$, so the bound $O\big(V(m^\ell)^e\big)$ gives the claim.
The same mechanism is applied to the [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), with chunk count $d$ as the parameter.

rounding-recovery.quote: Exact recovery by rounding works on the output of the [Synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) run in the opposite direction.
Exact recovery by rounding is based on the normalized cyclic convolution that [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) produces.
Exact recovery by rounding inherits its error from each [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), which ends with one truncation.
Exact recovery by rounding inverts the [Signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md), which evaluates the coefficients at $2^b$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: A simultaneous butterfly layer applies the [butterfly operation](butterfly-operation.md) to one selected address bit of every record at once.

The layer computes its chunk moves by the [linear network with restored auxiliary values](linear-network-exchange.md), which carries each input role to an output role with a prescribed sign and restores every auxiliary value.

The layer is formed as the [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of $D$ copies of the butterfly operation, one for each selected bit, acting on each coefficient and leaving the other address bits unchanged.

synthetic-transform.quote: It works in the [polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md).
It is built on $y$ as a [primitive root of unity](roots-of-unity.md) of order $2r$: $y^r=-1$, so $y^{2r}=1$, and no smaller positive power of $y$ equals $1$.
A synthetic polynomial transform generalizes the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) to a polynomial ring whose roots of unity are powers of $y$.

butterfly-operation: On column vectors this is multiplication by the matrix
The butterfly is not its own inverse.
Squaring the matrix gives $H_0^2=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}=\frac12 I$, where $I$ denotes the $2\times 2$ identity matrix.
So applying the butterfly twice returns the pair divided by two: $H_0(H_0(u,v))=\left(\frac u2,\frac v2\right)$.
Check with the example: $H_0(2,1)=\left(\frac32,\frac12\right)$, which is $\frac12(3,1)$.
The paper's transform calculation uses address rearrangements (moving stored values to other addresses), signed shifts (multiplying a value by a signed power of two), and the butterfly steps (cited).
kronecker-packing: Here $k$ also indexes coefficient positions, not transform positions.
Let $w = fg$ be the unreduced product, that is, before reduction modulo $y^r+1$, with coefficients $w_k = \sum_j f_j g_{k-j}$, where $k$ is the power of $y$ and the sum runs over $0 \le k-j < r$.
The integer product thus carries the product $w$, and the question is how to read its digits back.
If $\sum_k e_k B^k = \sum_k e'_k B^k$ with integers satisfying $|e_k|, |e'_k| < B/2$, then $e_k = e'_k$ for all $k$.
Each difference $e_k - e'_k$ has absolute value below $B$.
Let $m$ be the least index with $e_m \ne e'_m$.
Then $e_m - e'_m = -B\sum_{k>m} (e_k - e'_k) B^{k-m-1}$ is divisible by $B$, impossible since $0 < |e_m - e'_m| < B$.
$FG - w_0 = B\sum_{k\ge 1} w_k B^{k-1}$ is divisible by $B$, and $|w_0| < B/2$.
Since $B$ is even, $(-B/2, B/2]$ holds exactly one integer from each residue class modulo $B$, so $w_0$ is the balanced remainder of $FG$ modulo $B$.
Subtracting $w_0$ and dividing by $B$ leaves an expansion of the same form, so repeating the step gives $w_1, w_2, \dots$; uniqueness shows no other digits could give $FG$.
Finally, $y^r=-1$ gives $y^{k+r}=-y^k$, so $fg$ modulo $y^r+1$ has coefficients $w_k-w_{k+r}$ for $0\le k<r$, where $w_m=0$ for $m>2r-2$.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: big-O notation and worst-case time of Turing machines, polynomials and complex numbers, and the calculus the degree requires (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals). The same degree is taken to include introductory discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, induction, sets, graphs, recurrences) and a first course in linear algebra over the reals (vectors, subspaces, matrices, elimination, dot products), each at introductory depth. Fields in the abstract sense, tensor products, bilinear forms over general fields, Gaussian integers and the Chinese remainder theorem are not assumed.
